blocks.etymology: From soap + box. The figurative use of the word derives from the fact that soap products in the US used to be commonly transported to stores in large wooden boxes. It used to be common for individuals to give impromptu rally speeches to their neighbors by finding something to stand on like a soapbox.

thesaurus.definition: a crate for packing soap
a platform raised above the surrounding level to give prominence to the person on it

wiktionary.gloss: A crate for packing soap.

examples: The madman obtained a soapbox which he stood on at the corner of Broadway and Wall street, to shout out his prophecy of the end of the world.
wiktionary.gloss: A small platform, being or resembling a literal soapbox, on which a person stands in order to give an impromptu speech or espouse their views.

examples: The politician used Twitter as his soapbox.
Please stop using council meetings as your own personal soapbox.
wiktionary.gloss: A platform or outlet, such as a media platform, that a person uses to express their opinions.

examples: He's been on his soapbox all day about the new football coach.
wiktionary.gloss: A figurative means of talking repeatedly or at length about one's opinions on one's pet topic.

examples: His soapbox is the lack of public toilets in the city.
wiktionary.gloss: The topic itself.
A soapbox car.
